children: Faron Pharmaceuticals Ltd | Company announcement | October 19, 2026 at 09:15:00 EEST
Final data in PD-1 refractory metastatic melanoma underpin the rationale for the ongoing BLAZE trial of bexmarilimab in combination with nivolumab

Faron Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (AIM: FARN, First North: FARON), a global, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on creating innovative cancer treatments that leverage the patient’s own immune system, today announces that final results from the metastatic melanoma cohort of its Phase 1/2 MATINS study have been accepted as an ePoster at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026, taking place in Madrid, Spain, 23–27 October 2026.
These are the final results from the melanoma cohort of MATINS and the first report of complete survival data for all 25 patients, following interim results presented in 2022 and 2023.
The melanoma cohort comprised 25 patients with checkpoint inhibitor-refractory metastatic melanoma who received single-agent

at doses of 0.3 to 10 mg/kg every three weeks. All patients had failed prior anti-PD-1 therapy and 48% had also failed anti-CTLA-4 therapy. Patients had received a median of three prior lines of treatment, with a range of one to seven.

The disease control rate was 20% and median overall survival was 7.6 months (95% CI 5.3–14.9). Patients who achieved disease control had a median overall survival of 15.2 months, compared with 6.2 months in patients who did not (p=0.1545), and 12-month survival rates of 80% and 35% respectively. The duration of the previous line of therapy before entering the trial was similar in both groups (p=0.7275). Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 96% of patients, including grade 3 or higher events in 56% and serious events in 44%, consistent with a heavily pretreated metastatic population. Events assessed as related to
occurred in 36% of patients, most commonly fatigue (20%), with one patient (4%) experiencing a related event of grade 3 or higher.

Exploratory biomarker analyses showed lower baseline serum interferon gamma (sIFNγ) in patients who achieved disease control than in those who did not (3.5 versus 13.5 pg/mL, p=0.002). Low baseline sIFNγ was associated with a trend toward longer overall survival (10.1 versus 5.2 months, p=0.1971), and patients with disease control showed a median peak increase in sIFNγ of 181% on treatment, consistent with treatment-induced immune activation. These analyses are exploratory and the survival differences did not reach statistical significance in a cohort of this size.
Petri Bono, MD, PhD, Chief Medical Officer of Faron, stated, “These are the complete survival data for

in melanoma, in patients who had run out of options. One in five achieved disease control on a single agent, and those patients lived longer, although in 25 patients we cannot call that difference statistically significant. What interests us most is the biology underneath it. The patients who benefited started with lower interferon gamma and their levels rose on treatment, which is what we would expect if
is reactivating an immune response that had been switched off. That is the question the BLAZE trial is now asking in combination with a checkpoint inhibitor.”

BLAZE enrolls patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and melanoma who have progressed on prior anti-PD-1 therapy, and uses a sequential priming design in which patients receive an initial run-in dose of

is Faron’s wholly owned, investigational immunotherapy designed to overcome resistance to existing treatments and optimize clinical outcomes by targeting myeloid cell function. It binds to Clever-1, a receptor on immunosuppressive macrophages that helps cancer evade the immune system. By targeting Clever-1,
reprograms the tumor microenvironment to ignite a potent anti-tumor immune response.
The MATINS study was a first-in-human open label phase 1/2 clinical trial investigating the tolerability, safety and efficacy of

in ten different hard-to-treat metastatic or inoperable solid tumor cohorts, which are all known to host a significant number of Clever-1 positive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). The completed Part 1 of the trial dealt with tolerability, safety and dose escalation. The completed Part 2 focused on identifying patients who show an increased number of Clever-1 positive TAMs and exploring safety and efficacy. Data from MATINS showed
to be safe and well-tolerated, and demonstrated early signs of clinical benefit in patients who have exhausted all other treatment options.

Faron (AIM: FARN, First North: FARON) is a global, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, focused on tackling cancers via novel immunotherapies. Its mission is to bring the promise of immunotherapy to a broader population by uncovering novel ways to control and harness the power of the immune system. The Company’s lead asset is
, a novel anti-Clever-1 humanized antibody, with the potential to remove immunosuppression of cancers through reprogramming myeloid cell function.
